To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Bures distance is an effective metric for measuring the diversity of data distributions in feature space and (2) diversity matching using the Bures metric is an effective way to mitigate mode collapse in GAN training.

the Bures distance is a suitable metric to measure diversity in GANs and that matching the real batch diversity against the fake batch diversity can reduce mode collapse and improve the quality of the generated samples.

(a) diversity matching reduces mode collapsing and mode dropping substantially and has a strong positive effect on the quality of the generated samples; (b) the proposed diversity matching can be conveniently done by using the Bure's distance in either feature space (using the covariance matrix) or in kernel space (using the kernel matrix); (c) a simple training procedure that does not require any additional hyperparameters is proposed and tested on several datasets.
